title: De quibusdam eximiis proprietatibus circa divisores potestatum occurrentibus

deep.reconstruction:
This page closes the table of §35 (cases a = 23 to 30, non-squares only). For each base a it lists the residues ≡ 1 (mod 4) modulo 4a that sort odd primes p = 2m+1 into two classes. In the first class, p ≡ ±T (mod 4a) and p divides a^m − 1. In the second, p ≡ ±Θ (mod 4a) and p divides a^m + 1.

In modern terms, Euler's criterion gives a^((p−1)/2) ≡ (a/p) (mod p). So the T-classes are the residues t ≡ 1 (mod 4) with (a/t) = +1 and the Θ-classes those with (a/t) = −1. The Kronecker character (a/·) has conductor dividing 4a and is even, because a > 0. That is why p and 4a − p (the 'mp' sign) behave alike, and why each class contains exactly φ(4a)/4 residues.

Euler then remarks that everything is now clear, except that the two conclusions drawn from observation still need firm proofs. These are, in effect:
- the character depends only on p mod 4a and is even;
- the T-classes form a multiplicative subgroup.
This is the empirical content of quadratic reciprocity.

On p. 295 he restates the result as two theorems on prime divisors of binary quadratic forms, with gcd(x², ay²) = 1:
- (I) every prime divisor of x² − a y² is of the form 4as ± T. This is because (a/p) = 1.
- (II) every prime divisor of x² + a y² is of the form 4as + T or 4as − Θ. This is because (−a/p) = (−1/p)(a/p) = 1: for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) we need (a/p) = 1, giving +T; for p ≡ 3 (mod 4) we need (a/p) = −1, giving −Θ.
The page breaks off before the next 'Propositio'.

Verification of the entries:
- a = 23: QR mod 23 = {1,2,3,4,6,8,9,12,13,16,18}; all 11 T and 11 Θ entries are correct.
- a = 24: (6/p); 8 + 8 entries, correct.
- a = 26: (2/p)(p/13); 12 + 12 entries, correct.
- a = 27: T ≡ 1 (mod 12), Θ ≡ 5 (mod 12); 9 + 9 entries, correct.
- a = 29: QR mod 29; 14 + 14 entries, correct.
- a = 30: 8 + 8 entries, correct.
- a = 28: (7/p) = (p/7) for p ≡ 1 (mod 4). The T row should be 1, 9, 25, 29, 37, 53, 57, 65, 81, 85, 93, 109 (12 entries), but the print gives only 11 and omits 85. The Θ row (12 entries) is correct.
errors: Table, a = 28, T row: the residue 85 is missing. 85 ≡ 1 (mod 4), 85 ≡ 1 (mod 7), so (7/p) = +1 for p ≡ 85 (mod 112). Example: p = 197 = 112 + 85 has 28 a quadratic residue (14² = 196 ≡ −1, so 28 ≡ −1·(−28) ... more directly, 7 is a QR mod 197 because 197 ≡ 1 (mod 7)) and divides 28^98 − 1. The T row then has only 11 entries against 12 in the Θ row, breaking the φ(4a)/4 count Euler's own structure implies.
Typographical inconsistency: some rows print '±' and others '∓' for the same meaning 4as ± r. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Classification of primes p by whether p | a^m − 1 or a^m + 1 (p = 2m+1) according to p mod 4a, with p and 4a − p in the same class
ideas.modern_name: Euler's criterion combined with quadratic reciprocity / periodicity and evenness of the Kronecker character (a/·) mod 4a
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (conjectural form, 1744–1783); proved by Gauss 1801 (Legendre 1785/1798 partial)
ideas.where_published: E164 (Theoremata circa divisores numerorum in hac forma paa±qbb contentorum), E552 (Observationes circa divisionem quadratorum per numeros primos, Opuscula analytica 1783), and earlier sections of E557

ideas.what: Remark that the observational conclusions still lack demonstrations
ideas.modern_name: Need for a proof of the quadratic reciprocity law

ideas.what: Prime divisors of x² − ay² lie in 4as ± T, and those of x² + ay² lie in 4as + T or 4as − Θ
ideas.modern_name: Linear forms of prime divisors of binary quadratic forms, i.e. (±a/p) = 1 classes mod 4a

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine continuation of Euler's well-known empirical tables encoding quadratic reciprocity, followed by the standard restatement for divisors of x² ± ay². The only notable point is a small table omission (85 for a = 28), which the Opera omnia editors may already have corrected; I am unsure whether they did.
transcription_corrections: Theorem II should read '4as + T vel 4as − Θ'; the transcription's '[?]' marks the '+T' term, and 'alteruta' should be 'alterutra'.
a = 28, T row: the print indeed shows '...65, 81, / 93, 109,' with no 85. This omission is Euler's (or the printer's), not a transcription error.
In the a = 24, 26, 28 and 30 rows, '±' and '∓' are used interchangeably in the print; the meaning is 4as ± r in every case.
